sentences.text: Parabohaiornis is an extinct bird belonging to the Enantiornithes clade, specifically the Bohaiornithidae family, found in northeastern China.
Its upper jaw featured three teeth in the premaxilla and four teeth in the maxilla.
Unlike related genera, this species lacks a maxillary process on its nasal bone.
The acromion process is straight and parallel to the scapular shaft, differing from the deflected process seen in other bohaiornithids.
Parabohaiornis has a unique pygostyle-to-third-metatarsal length ratio ranging from 0.92 to 0.99.
In this bird, the proximal phalanx of the fourth digit is less than 70% the length of the penultimate phalanx.
The genus Parabohaiornis was named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor, and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014.
The name Parabohaiornis means "close to Bohaiornis", referring to its morphological similarity to that genus.
The species name martini honors the paleontologist Larry Dean Martin for his work on bird evolution.
Fossils of Parabohaiornis were collected near Lamadong Town in Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, from the Jiufotang Formation.
The known specimens are preserved in single slabs and housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
Both known specimens of Parabohaiornis represent subadult individuals, with the referred specimen being more mature than the holotype.
Phylogenetic analysis places Parabohaiornis as an advanced bohaiornithid closely related to the genus Bohaiornis.
The fossil record for Parabohaiornis spans the Aptian stage from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
